Uttarakhand CS Orders GIS Geo-Referencing of Water Supply Schemes After Jeolikote Contamination

2026-09-27 Garhwal Post Bureau GIS, geo-referencing, water supply, Uttarakhand, Jeolikote, mapping, Nainital, drinking water, infrastructure mapping
Read the source article

Quick summary

Following a contaminated drinking water incident in Jeolikote, Nainital, Uttarakhand's Chief Secretary ordered GIS geo-referencing and geo mapping of all major water supply schemes across the state, including sources, storage, pipelines, sewer lines, and crossing points.

Key takeaways

  • Chief Secretary Anand Bardhan directed geo mapping and GIS geo-referencing of all major water supply schemes across Uttarakhand
  • The mapping must cover the entire network from source to consumer, including storage, pipeline, sewer line, and crossing points
  • Physical verification of major water supply schemes must be completed within 15 days
  • The order follows a contaminated drinking water incident in Jeolikote, Nainital
  • CS expressed strong displeasure that despite a strong field network, information about contamination didn't reach state level in time
  • An effective information and feedback mechanism using field staff (teachers, patwaris, gram panchayat officials, tubewell operators) must be developed
  • SOP for checking drinking water and sewerage lines to be prepared and strictly enforced
